critique: The palette and central fiery texture are closer to the intended fire treatment, and there is a small vertical smoky suggestion in the core. However, the animation still reads overwhelmingly as a spark burst: from t1 to t4, numerous crisp glowing dots expand far outward in an almost radial field. The core remains clipped white and compact, while the desired result needs a sustained, larger, soft-edged haze/fire volume with much slower, coherent billowing motion rather than visible projectile-like embers.

suggestions.why: Greatly reducing emitter velocity prevents the fast explosion-like outward travel and lets the fire texture linger as a compact billowing volume.
Removing velocity variation suppresses the remaining wide radial spark distribution so motion follows the directed plume instead of ejecting in all directions.
A much lower emission rate reduces the dense field of individually readable ember dots, making the fire/smoke texture more legible.
Larger particles create more overlapping soft fire-and-smoke texture, expanding the hazy volume instead of presenting a tiny bright particle cluster.
